battle.name: 羅馬征服巴利阿里群島
battle.brief: 公元前三二三年，羅馬將領昆圖斯・凱基利烏斯・梅特盧斯奉命渡海征討巴利阿里群島，島上以投石著稱的部族在山丘上以石彈擊潰前一年羅馬艦隊。梅特盧斯改以包圍、攻城器械與石頭投射術反制，前一二一年攻下帕爾馬，梅諾卡守軍退入洞窟。卡面這具羅馬扭力式投石機即攻城器械的代表。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場戰爭是羅馬共和國對巴利阿里群島的征服戰役，交戰地是今西班牙巴利阿里群島中的馬略卡島與梅諾卡島，戰事橫跨公元前三二三年至前一二一年，最後以西元前一二一年梅特盧斯在群島得勝告終。羅馬方面的指揮體系由元老院授權的戰地統帥主持，兵員以羅馬公民軍團為骨幹，配以各部族提供的輔助步兵與輕裝投射兵，軍需由西班牙本土的港口基地供應，渡海運兵依靠羅馬的舊式划槳戰艦。巴利阿里人屬伊比利亞語系的島嶼部族，與半島上伊比利亞人同源而獨立發展，組織分散、以氏族為單位，沒有常備的城邦軍；其戰鬥核心是輕裝的投石手，人數眾多且技藝純熟，常佔據山丘與高地，以遮蔽物掩體，在數百步外以銅製或鉛製的球形石彈成齊射之陣，掩蓋己方攻擊兵接近。此外島上守軍亦使用伊比利亞式短彎刀、標槍與小型圓盾，並依海島地形在洞穴與岩臺設據。羅馬在群島的守備長期薄弱，僅有象徵性的駐軍與人質，故前一二二年執政官蓋爾維納斯與米努基烏斯・魯弗斯率艦隊前往追討欠繳的年貢時，才發現島民早已不受約束；海戰一敗，羅馬被迫以遠征軍的規模再來。戰後兩島被正式列為行省，島民解除武裝，其投石手則被收編進羅馬軍隊。
countriesEn: This war was the Roman Republic's conquest of the Balearic Islands, fought on Majorca and Menorca, the two principal islands of the Balearics in present-day Spain, and it ran from 123 BC to 121 BC, ending in Metellus's victory over the islands in 121 BC. On the Roman side the command structure was a field commander authorised by the Senate, with the citizen legions as the backbone of the army, supported by auxiliary infantry and light missile troops furnished by the tribes, and with supply coming from the harbour bases on the Spanish mainland while the crossing itself was made in Rome's old-fashioned rowing warships. The Balearic people belonged to the Iberian linguistic stock of the islands, related to the Iberians of the peninsula but developed independently, loosely organised by clan and without a standing civic army; the core of their fighting strength was the light-armed slinger, numerous and highly skilled, who habitually occupied the hills and heights, used cover, and from several hundred paces away delivered massed volleys of spherical stone missiles cast of bronze or lead to screen their own assault. The island defenders also used the Iberian falcata, javelins and a small round shield, and they sited strongholds in caves and on rock terraces in keeping with the terrain of an archipelago. Rome's garrison on the islands had long been thin, consisting of token troops and hostages, and so when the consuls Calvinus and Minucius Rufus sailed there in 122 BC to collect the arrears of tribute they found the islanders long since beyond control; after the naval defeat Rome was obliged to come back with an army of expedition scale. After the war both islands were formally constituted as a province, the islanders were disarmed, and their slingers were taken into Roman service.
people: 主導這場戰爭的羅馬將領是昆圖斯・凱基利烏斯・梅特盧斯。此人在元老院中的聲譽來自多次艱難的西班牙戰事；前一二二年海戰大敗後，執政官蓋爾維納斯與米努基烏斯・魯弗斯押著殘餘船艦退回本土，兵員的折損與威信的掃地迫使朝廷換人，於是公元前三二三年把群島的戰爭全權交給梅特盧斯。他當時尚未擔任執政官，也沒有攻島的經驗；梅特盧斯在島上的表現不在猛攻，而在於承認重步兵與攻城器械面對高地投石手難以施展，改為穩紮穩打、逐個拔除據點，並且在俘獲的巴利阿里人之手學會使用投石術，讓麾下部隊用對方的武器反過來壓制對方。三年之後他獲得「巴利阿里克」的尊號，於前一二一年凱旋，並在同一年擔任執政官。巴利阿里一方沒有留下可考的將領姓名，但群島的抵抗有兩種形態：一是前一二一年仍據守山巒與岩寨的部族，在羅軍封鎖退路、逐點攻破之後陸續放下武器；二是退入梅諾卡海邊洞穴的最後一批人，其首領在洞中率眾抵抗到底，直到羅軍封住洞口、以火攻洞，火勢吞沒洞口，退路亦被斷絕，餘者才出洞投降。歷史上巴利阿里人還有另一個廣為人知的身分，即為迦太基與漢尼拔效力的巴利阿里投石兵；他們在義大利戰場上的表現，使這個族名同時意味著精準、廉價而危險的遠程火力。羅馬在征服之後把這種人變成自己人，是這場戰爭在人事上最長久的結果。
peopleEn: The Roman general who shaped this war was Quintus Caecilius Metellus. His standing in the Senate came from a series of hard-fought campaigns in Spain; after the disastrous naval battle of 122 BC, when the consuls Calvinus and Minucius Rufus brought their surviving ships home with the army broken, the losses and the loss of face at court forced the Senate to change men, and in 123 BC the whole conduct of the war in the islands was handed to Metellus. He was not yet consul at that point and had no experience of fighting on an island; what he showed on the islands was not fury but judgement. He accepted that heavy infantry and siege engines could not operate against slingers holding the heights, and settled for a methodical advance that detached strongholds one by one, while learning the use of the sling from the Balearics he had captured and turning the enemy's own weapon against him. Three years later he earned the agnomen Balearicus, triumphed in 121 BC, and held the consulship in that same year. The Balearic side left no recorded names for its commanders, but the resistance of the islands took two forms: first, the clans still holding the mountains and rock forts in 121 BC, who laid down their arms one after another as the Romans sealed their retreats and broke position after position; second, the last men on Menorca, who withdrew into a sea cave and fought to the end under their own leader until the Romans closed the mouth of the cave and set fire to it, so that the flames took the entrance and the survivors came out only to surrender. The Balearics had another well-known identity in history, that of the Balearic slingers who served Carthage and Hannibal; the way they fought in Italy gave the name of the people a standing meaning for precision, cheapness and lethal range at distance. Rome's turning such men into its own after the conquest is the most durable human result of this war.
kits: 卡面這件投石機是羅馬的扭力式投石機 onager，公元前三世紀已在羅馬的攻城序列中服役，本役發生時它完全在役，因此有資格出現在島上的營盤與攻城線裡。卡面把它的原理概括為把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭；若說得更精確些，onager 的能量來自扭緊的簧束：以獸筋、亞麻或馬鬃絞成的束繩被絞到極限，固定在機架的兩支撐臂之間，投石臂隨之一端被拉低，扣上扳機後簧束猛然回彈，單臂在極短時間內掃過，把石彈加速射出，拋物線落點可以估算，威力因此有了可計算的破壞力；絞盤與配重則是更重型的重投石機所用的另一套機構，兩者常被混稱。攻城時 onager 立於工兵堆築的土壘之後，瞄準城牆的薄弱處反覆轟擊，配合藤架、雲梯與填平壕溝的土堤，攻打巴利阿里人的石砌山城。真正決定這場戰爭勝負的裝備卻是另一件：巴利阿里人的投石索（funda），以麻或亞麻搓成，末端繫皮兜，兜內裝三枚銅或鉛製的球形石彈，射手把皮兜繫在頭上甩動，取一臂之石彈拋出，射程可及數百步；羅軍在島上繳獲並仿製了這套索具，亦徵用島上少年自幼練習的傳統，練成一批羅馬本土的投石手，帝制時期軍團中常配備名為「巴利阿里克」的投石手分隊。除此之外，島上守軍用伊比利亞式短彎刀、標槍與小圓盾，羅軍則是標準的重裝配備：長方大盾、短劍、標槍與整套軍團甲胄；第五軍團（執政官馬略於前一〇四年為對抗辛布里人而招募的雲雀軍團）後來長期駐守群島，說明羅馬打算以常備軍而非遠征軍來長期控制這片海域。
kitsEn: The piece on the card is the Roman torsion catapult, the onager, already in service in the Roman siege list by the third century BC and therefore fully available when this war was fought, so it qualifies for the camps and the siege lines on the islands. The card sums up its principle as the conversion of the potential energy of a winch into a stone; stated more precisely, the energy of the onager comes from a tightly twisted bundle: cords of sinew, flax or horsehair are twisted to the limit and fastened between two upright posts of the frame, the throwing arm is drawn down at one end, and when the trigger is released the bundle snaps back, the single arm sweeping through in a very short time and hurling the stone with acceleration. The trajectory of the shot can be estimated, and the engine thus gave sieges a calculable destructive power. The winch and the counterweight belong to a different and heavier machine, the traction trebuchet, and the two are often confused with one another. In use, the onager stood behind a mound thrown up by the engineers, firing repeatedly at the thin points of a wall, and worked together with the vinea, the scaling ladders and earthen causeways filled across the ditches against the stone-built strongholds of the Balearics. The equipment that actually decided this war, however, was something else: the Balearic sling, the funda, twisted of hemp or flax, with a leather pouch at the end that carried three spherical stone missiles of bronze or lead. The slinger fastened the pouch round his head and whirled it, letting a missile fly with the swing of one arm to a range of several hundred paces. The Roman army captured such slings on the islands and had copies made, and took over the island practice of training boys from childhood, producing a body of Roman-born slingers; in the imperial period every legion commonly carried a detachment of slingers called balearici. Beyond that, the islanders fought with the Iberian falcata, javelins and a small round shield, while the Romans fought with the standard heavy kit: the long rectangular scutum, the gladius, the pilum and the full panoply of the legionary. That the Fifth Legion, the Alaudae raised by the consul Marius in 104 BC against the Cimbri, should afterwards be stationed on the islands for years shows that Rome intended to hold this sea with a permanent garrison rather than with an expeditionary force.
tactics: 島嶼戰爭的戰術關鍵是高低差。巴利阿里人善用馬略卡島多山的地形，把陣地設在石灰岩台地與山脊上，居高臨下，等羅軍進入開闊地才以密集石彈齊射；前一二二年執政官的艦隊在近岸拋錨後，正是因為船上的甲板成了毫無遮蔽的靶場，才被山上的投石手打得抬不起頭，一場順風突起的風暴更把殘餘羅兵捲入海中。梅特盧斯入島後的做法是放慢節奏：先以偵察與小股接觸摸清各據點的守備與取水路線，再以工兵築起圍牆式的土壘與藤架，把攻城器械推到可以射程之內，由 onager 對城牆與門樓作反覆的定向轟擊，再以輕裝步兵與工兵在掩體後接近，切入缺口，最後由重步兵列陣清剿。對付洞穴型據點，他用的是另一套辦法：先以投石與火箭封住洞口，再堆柴點火，讓退路與守軍一起被困。整場戰役因此不是一場會戰，而是三年之間對數十個據點的逐一攻取；海上由羅馬海軍切斷島民與西班牙本土之間的往來，島上則以羅軍的逐步推進與海軍封鎖合圍，使島民無法得到本土的支援，也無法把抵抗分散轉移到別處。羅軍在占領一地之後，會就地解散島上武裝、徵用投石手，再以羅馬式行政接管，使戰役的推進與治理同時進行。戰術上還有一項容易被忽略的變化：羅軍把敵人的投射技術收編為自己的，使原本屬於島民的火力優勢轉為羅軍的常備能力。
tacticsEn: The tactical key of an island war is the difference in height. The Balearics used the mountainous terrain of Majorca well, taking their positions on limestone terraces and ridges, holding the high ground and waiting until the Roman column had entered open ground before delivering massed volleys of stone. When the consuls' fleet anchored close inshore in 122 BC, the decks of the ships were a target with no cover at all, and the slingers on the hills above shot down the crews at their stations; a squall that sprang up with the wind then carried the remaining Romans off into the sea. Metellus' method after he landed was to slow the tempo down. He began with scouting and small contacts to learn the garrison of each post and the route by which it drew water, then had the engineers raise a wall-like mound and build the vinea, pushed the siege engines forward until they were within range, and had the onager batter the walls and the gate towers with directed shot; then light infantry and engineers moved up under cover, forced the breach, and the heavy infantry closed in to clear the position. Against cave strongholds he used another set of measures: first the mouth of the cave was sealed with stone shot and fire-darts, then brushwood was piled and lit, so that the retreat and the defenders were shut in together. The whole war was therefore not a single battle but a series of separate takings of strongholds over three years; at sea the Roman fleet cut the islanders off from the Spanish mainland, and on the islands the slow advance of the army together with the naval blockade enclosed them, so that they could draw no support from the mainland and could not shift their resistance elsewhere. After taking a place the Romans disbanded the local arms, enlisted the slingers, and handed the district over to Roman administration, so that advance and government went forward together. One more change in tactics is easily overlooked: the Roman army took over the enemy's missile technique as its own, so that the firepower advantage that had belonged to the islanders became a standing capacity of the Roman army.
data: 可以引用的數字大致如下。前一二二年的海戰，傳世記載提到參戰的巴利阿里輕裝兵約三萬人，羅馬艦隊幾近全滅，殘部退回西班牙本土的伊比沙島；此役之後元老院才改派梅特盧斯，戰役自公元前三二三年起算，到前一二一年梅諾卡的抵抗平定為止，前後約三年。群島幅員不大，馬略卡島面積約三千六百平方公里，梅諾卡島約七百平方公里，加上伊比沙島與外圍小島，羅軍面對的是分散在數百平方公里內的多個據點，而不是一座大城，因此三年戰期多花在攻取各個山寨與籌措糧秣上。羅軍的具體人數在現存記載中沒有留下確數，可以確知的是其核心為公民軍團，配以由西班牙各部族提供的輔助步兵與輕裝投射兵，並有工兵部隊隨行架設攻城器械；常駐群島的第五軍團按軍制當在一個大隊的規模，但這支部隊在征服完成時是否已隨梅特盧斯出師，記載並不明確。攻城器械的數量與性能同樣沒有可靠數字：onager 的射程與載重在不同估算中相差甚遠，其發射頻率取決於簧束疲勞與人工裝填速度，實戰中往往一日不過數十發至百餘發。相對而言，島上投石手的數量與戰果，歷來只有概數，流傳下來的說法強調其射速極快、單兵射程遠，一齊射即可瓦解密集縱隊，但具體數字不宜當作史實引用。
dataEn: The figures that can be given are roughly these. In the naval battle of 122 BC the transmitted accounts speak of about thirty thousand Balearic light troops engaged, and the Roman fleet was very nearly destroyed, the survivors making their way back to Ibiza on the Spanish mainland; only after that was the Senate content to change men and send Metellus, and the war is counted from 123 BC to the final pacification of Menorca in 121 BC, about three years in all. The islands are not large: Majorca covers roughly 3,600 square kilometres and Menorca roughly 700, and with Ibiza and the smaller islets the Romans were facing a number of separate positions spread over several hundred square kilometres rather than one great city, which is why three years went mostly on taking the hill forts one by one and on moving food and water. No reliable figure survives for the size of the Roman force; what can be said is that its core was the citizen legions, with auxiliary infantry and light missile troops furnished by the tribes of Spain, and with engineers travelling with it to build and serve the siege engines. The Fifth Legion, which was to be stationed on the islands, would in theory have numbered about a cohort, but whether it went out with Metellus at the close of the campaign is not clearly recorded. The numbers and performance of the siege engines are equally uncertain: estimates of the range and the weight of shot of the onager differ widely, and its rate of fire depended on the fatigue of the torsion bundle and on the speed of manual loading, in practice perhaps a few dozen shots a day up to a hundred or more. On the other side, the numbers and the results of the Balearic slingers survive only as rough statements, with the tradition emphasising the speed of their shooting and the reach of a single man, a massed volley being enough to break up a dense column; the precise figures should not be quoted as history.
cause: 開戰的起因是巴利阿里人沒有履行兩項義務。公元前二四一年羅馬在第一次布匿戰爭末期取得群島的控制權，巴利阿里人曾向羅馬提供人質，承諾停止對西班牙本土的襲擾並按年繳納貢賦；此後數十年裡，島上的襲擾與劫掠並未真正停止，羅馬的商船與西班牙沿岸的聚落在一個世代中反覆受襲，欠繳的貢賦也越積越多。前二三七年羅馬曾在迦太基人希耶羅指揮下的一場戰役中打敗過島上聯盟，強迫其簽下以白銀支付年金的條約，此後羅馬的稅吏年年上島催收，衝突便由零星的劫掠變成有組織的清欠。然而真正把兩個勢力推上刀鋒的是前一二二年那一場海戰：執政官蓋爾維納斯與米努基烏斯・魯弗斯以為羅馬的艦隊足以壓服島民，結果在近岸遭高地方向的投石齊射重創，幾乎全軍覆沒，兩人帶著殘兵退回本土。慘敗迫使羅馬把這場戰爭升級：既然島上無法用一次遠征解決，就必須真正登陸、真正奪取島嶼並把島民編入自己的軍隊。除了報復與清欠，深層的動機是戰略的——控制馬略卡與梅諾卡等於握住西班牙海岸與義大利之間的海路，也等於能從西班牙的礦山運出羅馬新征服省份所需的資源；在羅馬剛於西西里與西班牙站穩腳跟、而迦太基勢力剛被削弱之際，任何能威脅這條航線的勢力都不能容忍。更關鍵的是，這群島的居民提供了羅馬眼下最缺的一種兵種：能作精密遠程投射的輕裝步兵。
causeEn: The immediate cause was that the Balearics had not honoured two obligations. In 241 BC, as the First Punic War drew to its close, Rome gained control of the islands, and the Balearics gave hostages to Rome, promising to stop their raids on the Spanish coast and to pay an annual tribute; over the decades that followed the raids and the plunder did not really stop, Roman ships and the settlements along the Spanish coast were hit again and again through a whole generation, and the arrears of tribute grew. In 237 BC the Romans broke the island coalition in a campaign fought under the Carthaginian Hiero and forced a treaty paying an annual indemnity in silver, and Roman tax collectors then came to the islands every year to collect it, so that the conflict changed from scattered plunder into organised collection of debts. But what truly drove the two powers to the sword was the naval battle of 122 BC. The consuls Calvinus and Minucius Rufus believed that the fleet would overawe the islanders; instead it was cut up on the coast by massed stone from the heights and was very nearly wiped out, and the two men led the broken remnant home. The disaster obliged Rome to raise the scale of the war: if the islands could not be settled by a single raid, then Rome would have to land properly, take the islands properly, and enlist the islanders into its own army. Beyond revenge and the collection of debts lay a strategic motive. Holding Majorca and Menorca meant holding the sea road between the Spanish coast and Italy, and it meant being able to bring out of the Spanish mines what the provinces Rome had just conquered needed; at a moment when Rome had only just established itself in Sicily and Spain and the power of Carthage had just been broken, no power that could threaten that road could be tolerated. Most important of all, the islanders could supply Rome with the one kind of soldier it most lacked, light infantry able to make long-range precision shots.
impact: 這場戰爭最深遠的影響不在土地，而在兵種。羅馬從此擁有了一種能以極低費用取得極高壓迫力的投射兵力：巴利阿里投石手被整編成獨立的輔兵分隊，以 cohors Balearum 之名附屬於各個軍團，帝制時期常見的做法是每個軍團配備約一百二十名巴利阿里投石手；拉丁文中的 balearus 從此成了投石手的代稱，義大利與高盧的軍鎮中也就留下了這個名號，羅馬軍的作戰手冊與軍械清單裡都把它列為標準配備之一。這種把被征服者的專長收編為帝國常備技術的做法，之後在越內高盧戰爭、對抗敘利亞的戰役以及遠征不列顛時一再重演，構成了羅馬擴張的典型模式。群島本身則被改造成安寧的行省：巴利阿里島的綿羊在羅馬紡織業中以細軟羊毛著稱，島上的產成品隨商船運往羅馬；島民被解除武裝，編入羅馬的行政與軍事秩序，拉丁語與羅馬式城市生活逐漸取代舊有的部族結構，馬略卡島上的帕爾馬在征服後重建，成為島上的羅馬式據點。此後群島的戰略價值仍不斷被重新確認：公元前七十一年的塞托里烏斯曾以梅諾卡島為反抗羅馬的基地，公元前四十五年凱撒的內戰又把島上勢力捲入本國的爭鬥。從地中海的整體格局看，這場戰爭標誌著羅馬把西班牙方向的海域完全握在手中，迦太基在巴利阿里一帶的殘餘影響被徹底清空。
impactEn: The most far-reaching effect of this war lay not in land but in a kind of soldier. Rome now possessed a missile force that bought enormous pressure at very small cost: the Balearic slingers were organised into separate auxiliary detachments attached to the legions under the name cohors Balearum, and the usual arrangement in the imperial period was for each legion to carry about a hundred and twenty Balearic slingers; balearus became in Latin a synonym for the slinger, the name stuck in the garrison towns of Italy and Gaul, and it was entered as one of the standard items in the Roman order of battle and in the lists of service equipment. This practice of turning the special skill of the conquered into a standing technique of the empire was repeated afterwards in the campaigns in Transalpine Gaul, in the wars against Syria and in the invasion of Britain, and it became a typical mode of Roman expansion. The islands themselves were remade as a quiet province: the Balearic sheep were famous in the Roman textile trade for their fine wool, and the produce of the islands travelled to Rome with the merchant ships. The islanders were disarmed and drawn into the Roman administrative and military order, Latin and Roman town life gradually replacing the old tribal structure, and Palma on Majorca was rebuilt after the conquest as the Roman-style centre of the island. The strategic value of the islands was confirmed again and again afterwards: Sertorius used Menorca as a base for resistance to Rome in 71 BC, and the civil wars of Caesar in 45 BC drew the island's factions into the quarrels of the Roman world. Seen from the wider Mediterranean, this war marked the point at which Rome held the seas toward Spain entirely in its own hands and the last traces of Carthaginian influence in the Balearics were swept away.
result: 前一二一年，戰役以巴利阿里人的全面屈服告終。梅特盧斯先後攻取馬略卡島上的帕爾馬等據點，再把殘局推向梅諾卡：島上最後一批守軍退入海邊的洞穴堅守，羅軍封堵洞口並縱火，洞中的抵抗者與洞穴同毀，未能出洞者葬身火海，餘者出洞投降，連同家眷一起被解除武裝。前一二一年梅特盧斯為此舉行凱旋式，並從此獲得巴利阿里克的稱號；群島隨後被正式編入羅馬行省，島上的投石手被大批收編進羅馬軍隊，成為帝國投射兵力的來源之一。結果有兩面：就軍事而言，羅馬用三年時間結束了一場從前以為可以靠一次艦隊遠征解決的麻煩，島上再沒有能威脅西班牙海岸的獨立武裝，航線與礦產的通道被打通，羅馬得以把常備軍駐紮於群島，長期監控地中海西部的交通。就文化與軍事技術而言，巴利阿里人用自己的血換來了一個永久的位置：他們的投射技藝從此不再是對手的所有物，而是羅馬軍的標準裝備，寫進了軍團的編制、薪餉與榮譽之中，隨著羅馬的每一次遠征被帶到更遠的地方。從更長的時間尺度看，這場戰爭的真正收尾並不在前一二一年，而在其後：群島被納入帝國的行省秩序，島民被同化，舊有的部族結構瓦解，而那支以投石聞名的隊伍則以羅馬軍團編制中一個固定分隊的形式，繼續存在了數百年。
resultEn: In 121 BC the war ended in the complete submission of the Balearics. Metellus took in turn Palma on Majorca and the other strongholds, and then drove the end-game onto Menorca, where the last defenders withdrew into a sea cave and held it; the Romans sealed the mouth of the cave and set fire to it, the resistance and the cavern were destroyed together, those who could not come out were buried in the fire, and the rest came out and surrendered, their families with them, and were disarmed. Metellus celebrated his triumph in 121 BC and took the name Balearicus; the islands were then formally constituted as a Roman province, and large numbers of the Balearic slingers were taken into Roman service, becoming one of the sources of the empire's missile strength. The result had two faces. Militarily, Rome had settled in three years a business that had been thought could be dispatched by a single fleet raid: no independent armed force on the islands was left to threaten the Spanish coast, the sea road and the channel for minerals were open, and Rome was able to station a permanent garrison on the islands and keep watch over the traffic of the western Mediterranean for the long term. In cultural and military-technical terms, the Balearics bought themselves a permanent place with their blood: their missile skill ceased to be a possession of the enemy and became standard equipment of the Roman army, written into the organisation, the pay and the honours of the legion, and carried to ever more distant places by every Roman expedition. On the longer time scale the real conclusion of this war does not lie in 121 BC but in what came after: the islands were taken into the provincial order of the empire, the islanders were assimilated, the old tribal structure dissolved, and the company that had been famous for the sling went on existing for several hundred years as a fixed detachment in the organisation of the Roman legion.
